en: A long, long conflict, the\nbeginning of which is uncertain,\nthe Holy Land War.

A flame that smolders and
burns between the Schenberyl
continent's two great powers:
the Kingdom of Rubarika and
the Baschen Empire.

In their struggle over the "Holy
Land of Asyl," these two
powers have sent countless
people to the front lines of the
Holy Land War throughout
history.

Nations, people, and lands alike
have been exhausted to their
absolute limits by wars
spanning countless years.
And yet, the fighting cannot\nstop; it cannot be stopped.

For if they were to stop or
retreat, the enemy
nation―locked in a conflict with
no certain beginning―would
gain overwhelming power.
The "Messenger of Daftes."
That overwhelming power is\nbrought forth by an existence\nknown by that name.

He who wins the Holy Land
War and claims Asyl earns the
honor of welcoming the
"Messenger of Daftes,"
descending via the "Moonlight
Ladder.

Throughout history, the
"Messenger of Daftes" has
brought superhuman blessings,
power, and wisdom to both
Rubarika and Baschen.

To welcome more "Messengers
of Daftes" is the supreme
mandate and very essence of
both Rubarika and Baschen.

So, that's the gist of the Holy
Land War that <font color=yellow>Rubarika</font> and
<font color=yellow>Baschen</font> have been fighting
over for years.

Huh... I thought a "Holy Land
War" meant a religious conflict,
but it seems more about
practical benefits.

You really didn't know, did
you? I thought even the small
neighboring countries were
aware of it.

U-Um, well, we don't stay in
one place for long, so we rarely
get the chance to hear stories
about history and things like
that!
Hmm.

Both Rubarika and Baschen
have many legends of the Holy
Land War, but they don't use
them for their performances.

W-War stories are usually
pretty sad, right!? Our selling
point is being incredibly
cheerful! Ahahaha...
Ah... Yeah, that makes sense. I\nguess that's a valid reason.
(She's being cornered by her\nown lies.)
(Yeah... Eve is sweating a lot.)

Anyway, the Holy Land War is
intensifying right now. Because
of that... public order has
deteriorated like this.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font>: Phew... You guys really
are strong. Those weapons and
mechanisms aren't just for
show, are they?
<font color=blue>Verda</font>: Do not be so surprised.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font>: I am surprised. To be
blunt, you possess something
extraordinary. Such things
don't usually circulate in this
world.
<font color=blue>Verda</font>: What do you mean by\nthat?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font>: I mentioned it earlier.\nAbout the <font color=yellow>"Servant of Daftes"</font>.

The winner of the Holy Land
War gains <font color=yellow>"Servant's Power"</font>,
which contains something
similar to what Verda
possesses.
Even Tika's mechanical arm is\nlike that.
<font color=blue>Eve</font>: What do you mean?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font>: It's exactly what it\nsounds like... It's like a so-called\nblessing from the gods.

The "Servant of Daftes"
provides things that Rubarika
or Baschen could never create
with their own power.

<font color=blue>Eve</font>: I don't quite understand...
but I can see why people would
go to war to get their hands on
something like that.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Is that so, Euwin? Is\nyours also a "Servant's\nPower"?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Huh? Oh, this? Ah... no,\nthis is different.
This is... well, something I\nreceived from a person.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> I see...

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Anyway, the Holy Land
War has caused bandits and
"Baschen Beasts" to roam free,
leaving public order in total
chaos.
Euwin, why were you at\nDagris?

Ah, it's because the village of
Dagris sent a petition asking
for help with the security in
the surrounding area.
Come to think of it, a child\nfrom the village mentioned\nthat.
But would they really dispatch\nthe lord's son all by himself for\nthat?
They wouldn't. Naturally.
...What do you mean?

When the villagers of Dagris
came to petition, I happened to
be summoned to my family
home.

Having traveled around and
seen so much damage caused
by Baschen beasts, I told them
we should grant the petition.

But my father, the lord, and my
eldest brother just laughed.
They said the current Carlone
can't afford such luxuries.

...Even though they're sending
mountains of soldiers to the
front lines of the Holy Land
War.
Euwin...
I was getting sick of my\nbrother's lecturing anyway, so...

Both my father and brother
constantly nagged me to act in
a way that wouldn't shame the
Rakstar name,
So I came here to do\nsomething worthy of the\nRakstar family. That's all.
...It is what they call Noblesse\nOblige.
Noble...s?
Noblesse Oblige is a term that\nsymbolically represents an\nethical standard:

That those who possess
privilege are recognized for
their existence by fulfilling their
duties to those who do not.
Hmm. I don't really get it, but\nEuwin, you're amazing!

It's nothing like that. It's just a
side project of my adventure.
A way to test my skills. A test
of skills...
Wait, I just heard a strange\nvoice...

Aaaaah!! But! The Village Chief
was so grateful before you left!
You don't have to act shy and
call it a "test of skills"!
What's wrong?
It's not "acting" shy. I am\ngenuinely embarrassed.
Huh?
In this Holy Land War, Rubarika\nholds a significant advantage.

Because of that, noble houses
are racing to send people to
the front for post-war honors
or the "Power of the
Messenger.
As a result, no territory is able\nto properly maintain public\norder,

Leaving bandits like those from
earlier, or the "Beasts of
Baschen" that crossed the
border, running wild.

And yet, the Rakstar family
won't even protect a single
village. Nobles only exist
because of their people.

I'm ashamed my family just
watched as their fifth son―the
black sheep―tried to play the
hero alone under the guise of a
village inspection.

And that I'm the only one who
has to go and protect the
village. As a member of the
Rakstar family, I'm ashamed.
...What a remarkable young\nman.
...True. Even if that personality\ntends to get him into trouble.

Don't remind me. I know. I'm
perpetually broke since I'm
neither at an age nor in a
position to get an allowance
from my family.
So, I'm counting on the reward.
Come on, the road ahead to\nCarlone City is going to be\nquite tough. Let's stay focused.
Yes... It seems you're carrying\na very heavy burden as well,\nEuwin.
You likely know much more\nthan most. We shall count on\nyour guidance.
Tika's safety is the top priority.\nI want you to remember that.
Rekoro. I'll be fine.
We know. We have taken that\nto heart ourselves. We will not\nlose sight of our priorities.
I hope we can uncover more\ntruths, bit by bit.
For now, let's follow Euwin.\nFirst, we have to reach Carlone\nCity!
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Phew... Even though we\ncame from Dagris, that was a\npretty intense checkpoint.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> Indeed. Without Euwin's
Rakstar crest, there's no telling
what nonsense they would
have put us through.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Those soldiers were\nscary...

<font color=blue>Eve</font> The Captain is right. The
war has soldiers on edge,
which might be why public
order is worsening.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> But they didn't say\nanything about Verda's gun or\nmy Arms.
Perhaps it's because everyone\nknows about the "Power of the\nMessenger."

<font color=blue>Eve</font> A lot of this feels
unsettled... I'm feeling uneasy,
so I want Euwin to come back
quickly.
He left immediately after the\ncheckpoint was finished, but I\nwonder what happened.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> said he'd arrange our
travel permits before we left,
but I wonder if something went
wrong...
Speak of the devil.
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Hey, sorry to keep you\nwaiting. ...Things got a little\ncomplicated, so I'm late.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> What do you mean,\ncomplicated?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> The eastern highway\nleading to the Royal Capital is\nblocked.

Apparently, a massive number
of "Baschen Beasts" have
appeared. Travel is prohibited
for a while during the sweep
operation.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Is there no other way to\nthe Royal Capital?

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> There are others, but I
wouldn't recommend them. You
all are already people of
questionable identity.

Being traveling performers
during wartime is practically an
invitation to be suspected of
being spies.

Rakstar's name works in some
places but not others. Unless
every second counts, it's
better to wait here.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> True enough. Though,\nconsidering Tika, we cannot\nafford to linger too long.
Is there no way we could just\nexterminate those beasts\nourselves and call it a day?

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Hey, don't be
unreasonable. The knights
guarding the city walls and
highways have taken heavy
casualties.

I know you're strong, but as
your guide, I can't force you to
stick your heads into danger.
Please, bear with it.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> This is a problem.

<font color=blue>Tika</font> Euwin-onichan is using his
name to help us out in so many
ways, so you shouldn't push
him too hard.
I'll be fine, so why don't we wait\na little?
<font color=blue>Verda</font> ...Hmm, it seems we\nwere being quite immature.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> ...You're right. I'm sorry,\nEuwin.
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> I appreciate your\nunderstanding. I'm going to\nscout the city a bit more.
I've already arranged an inn, so\nif you decide to rest, please go\nto the one on this note.
Also, you're free to explore the\ncity, but please try not to\nstand out.
For now, let's meet up at the\ninn during dinner. See you then.

Hmm... they certainly provide
everything one could need. It
would be best to avoid doing
anything that might trouble
Euwin.
You're right. Let's just stay\nquiet and wait for the blockade\nto be lifted.
What's the plan, Captain? Want\nto take a stroll through town?
It looks like this is the North\nGate. In that case, can we only\ngo West, East, or South?
Go West
Go South
Go East
Return to the North Gate
Rest at the Inn Today
It seems the west is the\ndistrict where the wealthy\nreside.
There are so many soldiers.

From the looks of it, none of
the soldiers are carrying
anything like Verda's gun or
Tika's Arms.

Rekoro, can you detect
anything that doesn't match
the civilization level of this
planet?

No devices or gadgets that
defy the current civilization
level have been detected
within scanning range.

True. Euwin said it was quite
rare too, so maybe only
high-ranking military officers
have them.

Look over there, that flag has
the same pattern as the Gem
Euwin showed at the city wall
checkpoint. That might be the
mansion of the Rakstar family,
the lords of Carlone.
Approaching them would surely\narouse suspicion. It would be\nbest to withdraw.
We were on the west side,\nright? Where are we going\nnext?
The south seems to be the\ncenter of the city's industry.
There are so many shops!
But it's not very lively. I don't\nsee anyone out shopping at all.

Whether it's the war or blocked
roads to the capital, it looks
like we won't be able to enjoy
any casual shopping.
Huh? Isn't that Euwin over\nthere?
You're right. I wonder what he's\ndoing in front of a closed shop.
Perhaps he had something he\nwanted to buy, but it was their\nday off.
Oh, he left. I wonder what kind\nof shop it was.

A sign with a drawing of a
hand with the index finger
raised... I have no idea what
kind of shop that is.

We don't need to force
gathering resources right now,
so there's nothing left for us to
do here. Shall we explore
somewhere else?
This was the south side, right?\nWhere are we going next?
The east seems to be a\nresidential area.
But it's already evening, and\nthere aren't many houses with\nthe lights on.

You're right. There's no smoke
coming from the chimneys
either... I wonder if no one lives
here.

The balance between the
number of biological heat
signatures and the number of
dwellings is extremely poor.

I infer that there are a
considerable number of vacant
houses if we move from the
main street to the back alleys.
I wonder what could be the\ncause.

Even in dwellings with biological
heat signatures, many show no
detectable heat source from
fuel.

I suspect that the shortage of
supplies due to the highway
blockade is causing disruptions
to daily life.

I wonder if the blockade has
been going on for quite a while.
If it's something we can fix, I'd
love to help them out...
But Euwin said we shouldn't\ncause any trouble, so we can't\ndo that.

Come to think of it, he did say
that the gate leading to the
Royal Capital is located on this
eastern side.
Huh? I felt like I just saw\nEuwin... Was it just my\nimagination?
In any case, it seems unlikely\nwe will find anything of value\nhere.
And I don't want to draw any\nsuspicion by talking carelessly\nto the gatekeepers.
This was the eastern side,\nright? Where are we going\nnext?
The northern gate closes in\nthe evening, it seems.
I wonder if the people of Dagris\nare going to be okay...
I overheard something earlier;\nit sounds like a security force\nhas been dispatched.
Really! Oh, thank goodness!

The blockade to the Eastern
Royal Capital is a major reason,
too. If the "Beasts" ravage the
north, the town will be
completely isolated.
So they finally decided to take\naction. A blessing in disguise, I\nsuppose.
Still, I wonder what exactly the\n"Beasts of Baschen" are.

Do you think the "Beasts" near
Dagris are related to the
rumors of many more on the
eastern highway?
They may not be unrelated...\nthough there is no way for us\nto know for certain right now.

Regardless, the safety of the
people in Dagris has been
secured, so we'll just have to
be content with that for now.
It's getting late. Shall we move\non?
This is the northern gate,\nright? Where are we going\nnext?
Right. Let's head toward the\ninn Euwin arranged for us.
This inn is even more luxurious\nthan I expected.
The bed is so fluffy!

Eve: We really must thank
Euwin. I feel like all the fatigue
from our journey is just melting
away.
Tika, are you feeling alright?
Yeah! I'm fine! Right, Rekoro?

Affirmative. While some slight
depletion of physical stamina is
observed, no major
abnormalities are detected.
If Tika is alright, shall we have\na brief strategy meeting before\nEuwin returns?
<font color=blue>Eve</font> That's true. I am curious to\nknow what Carlone's town\nlooks like from space. Coro.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "..."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Coro?

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "...Since you haven't been
talking to me much, I thought
you'd forgotten all about me.
What is it, Eve?"
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Why are you sulking? It\nis quite immature.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> That's right. There's no\nway I could talk to you in front\nof Euwin.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Hmph! Hmph!"

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Captain, I must suggest
that Coro's excessive emotions
may hinder stable operations
and threaten Tika's safety.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Hmph!! Fine! I don't care!
I'm just a useless AI whose
only redeeming quality is being
creepy-cute anyway!"
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Coro... I'm sorry. Were you\nlonely?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "...Hmph."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Coro! Stop sulking already!\nTika is even apologizing to you!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "...So, what was it you\nneeded me for?"

<font color=blue>Eve</font> Good grief! I'm asking if the
long-range sensors detect
anything strange in Carlone
City from space!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "There's nothing unusual\nat all~"
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Coro! Take this seriously!

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "I'm being serious! I can
only detect things in Carlone
City that match this planet's
average civilization level!

At the very least, I'm not
detecting anything like the
"Servant of Daftes" or the
"Servant's Power" that Euwin
mentioned!"
<font color=blue>Eve</font> ...I see.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> "What about Baschen's\nbeasts? Well, in short,\nThornites."

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Regarding that, I can't
detect any biological
signatures on the highways
toward the Royal Capital that
Euwin mentioned which are
large or numerous enough to
have caused damage to the
Knights."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> What do you mean?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "I have successfully\ntracked the subjugation force\ndispatched from Carlone City.

There's a large forest along
the highway where the beasts
should be, but I can't find any
signs of them anywhere.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> It's not interference waves\nagain, is it? It's not like there's\na Pulse Tower nearby.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "I don't think that's the\ncase, but...

I can't distinguish Thornites
from others without optical
sensors, so frankly, I can't
judge what's happening on the
ground.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Hmm. Perhaps we will\nknow more once Euwin returns.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "About that... instead of
waiting for the blockade to lift,
why not just teleport straight
to the Rubarika Royal Capital?
<font color=blue>Eve</font> That's true, but Euwin's\nguidance is invaluable.

There's a world of difference
between heading to the Royal
Capital blindly and going with
guidance.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> Indeed. This town shows
the unsettling effects of war
everywhere. The Royal Capital
may not be any safer.

With Euwin to guide us, we can
at least reduce the risk of
being treated as suspicious
persons.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Tika.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Yeah.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Do you know anything\nregarding the Holy Land War?
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Anything beyond what big\nbrother Euwin told me...

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> I presume that at Tika's
age, she would not have had
the opportunity to learn the
details.

This vessel also has no
recorded data that could
update the basic information
regarding Ewin Laxter.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> I'm sorry...
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Don't apologize. It's not\nyour fault, Tika.
From now on, if you notice\nanything or feel even a little\nuneasy, you must tell us, okay?
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Okay...

<font color=blue>Eve</font> Anyway, we'll follow Euwin
tomorrow and head for the
Rubarika Royal Capital once
the highway blockade is lifted.

Coro, you're not to make a
sound unless it's absolutely
necessary. Euwin will get
suspicious!
<font color=blue>Verda</font> I wonder if Coro is even\ncapable of such a feat.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "That's easy! If push\ncomes to shove, I'll just say it's\nthe Captain's ventriloquism!"

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Captain, I advise
caution. Your ship AI, Coro, has
an algorithm that causes it to
become sulky if not spoken to
regularly.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Rekoro-san! If you say\nthings like that, I really will get\nsulky!"
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Hold on, it looks like\nEuwin has returned. We shall\nspeak later.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Geez...!"
Sorry I'm late. ...Was anyone\nelse in this room just now?
Eh!? N-no one was here!?
I see... I thought I heard a\nvoice, though...
Oh well. Phew, maybe I'm just a\nlittle tired.
Euwin, are you okay?
Yeah, sorry, don't worry...

About the eastern highway
blockade, it won't be lifted
soon. It seems they're
struggling with the subjugation.
So, it looks like you'll have to\nstay in this town for a bit\nlonger.
Hmm. It cannot be helped.
Carlone, this isn't a bad town. I\nhope you enjoy your stay. Well,\nI'm going to bed now...
O-okay.
You seemed strangely rushed.

I see. Captain, you're in the
same room as Euwin, right? If
he doesn't seem well, please
look after him.
...Brother Euwin...
Eh?
Captain. Do you need\nsomething from Rekoro?
...Alright. They're asleep.
Sorry. I'll come back as soon\nas I can.
I have to hurry...!
Where are you going?
!? Tika!
...Are you going to fight the\n"Beasts" on the highway all by\nyourself?
...Ugh... Ah, I'm in trouble. I\ndidn't think you'd notice me...
Even though you said it was\nimpossible just a moment ago.

Circumstances have changed.
It seems a hot-headed friend
of mine is about to do
something reckless.
A friend?
One of the very few friends I\ntruly trust.
An eccentric person who\ncrafted this weapon for me.
In that case, maybe Eve and\nthe others could come along\ntoo...

This is a personal matter. I
can't involve you all in this.
That goes for you as guides,
too.

I'll be back by morning. I
promise not to be reckless. So,
please just wait for me without
a word...
Even saying that, it doesn't\nlook like you'll listen.
...Ehehe.

That's why I'm telling you now.
It's no use trying to wake
everyone up. I am a citizen of
Rakstar.
I can pass the checkpoint at\nany hour, but you won't be able\nto, even if I'm with you.
Euwin...

Hehe. You're all too kind. If I
didn't say something like this,
you'd never give up. Well then,
I'm off.
Rekoro.
Captain, you were awake.
...Yeah! I get it.
Eve! Verda! Coro! Wake up!
*Pant*... *pant*... That idiot...\njust how deep did he wander\nin...?

The camp folk haven't seen
him either. Besides, how can
we not even know where the
beast pack is...?
Agh!
Damn... that was close.
This is strange... they're much\nstronger than the ones near\nDagris.
He'd better be safe... I told him\nto at least wait until I got back!
...! Over there!?
What!? Wh-when did it get\nhere!? Where did something\nthis huge even come from!
Whoa!?
Damn it! It's huge but so fast!\nAt this rate...!
Summon Comet!!
Euwin! Are you alright!
Big brother! Are you hurt!?
Y-you guys, what are you doing\nhere!?
We'll talk later! Right now, we\nhave to deal with this swarm of\nThornite!
R-right!
We managed to defeat them\nsomehow.
...You really saved me. I would\nhave been finished if I were\nalone. Thank you.
Before that, don't you have\nsomething to say to Tika and\nus?
Big brother Euwin...!
...Yeah. I'm sorry for leaving\nwithout a word. And for trying\nto keep it a secret.
Big brother Euwin, we're friends\nnow. So... if you're ever in\ntrouble, please talk to me.
I might not be able to do much\nto help, though.
...Friends, huh? It feels strange.\nI haven't really had many of\nthose until now.
That's right. It's not about how\nmuch time you've spent\ntogether!
I'm so glad you're safe, big\nbrother Euwin. Now let's go\nsave our friends quickly!
Yeah. Thank you. It's good to\nofficially meet you.

But how on earth did you all
get through the checkpoint?
The security should be
especially tight at this hour...
Hmm? Well, they say even the\njudgments of hell come full\ncircle in the end.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> We've been waiting,
Captain. We're tracing Euwin's
coordinates; he's moving
deeper into the forest.

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> A landing point
approximately one hundred
meters away from Ewin Laxter
is deemed optimal.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> I agree. Carlone's
subjugation force is circling the
forest at a distance and has
not ventured into the interior.

Until morning, the light of
teleportation within a
hundred-meter radius of Euwin
should not be noticed.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Can't you find where\nEuwin's friends are?

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Visibility is poor in this
forest, making it hard to track
untagged locals. We have no
idea who they are...
<font color=blue>Eve</font> That means we have no\nchoice but to go down there\nand save them!
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Let's go, hurry!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Just to confirm, Rekoro,\nis it alright to deploy Rekoro\nand Tika?

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> As a life-saving pod AI,
I have reservations about
deploying Tika to an area with
a high probability of combat.

However, if Ewin Laxter is lost,
the objective of Tika returning
to her home, the original
Daftine, will drift further away.

Verda Kleiman's device is
highly reliable. All things
considered, I will not oppose
Tika's descent into the area.

...Besides, even if I opposed it,
they likely wouldn't listen. An AI
should focus on considering
the next best course of action.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Ehehe... sorry.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> The people on this ship
really do rush headlong into
danger; as an AI, I never get a
moment's peace.
<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> I agree.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> That's right. There's no
time for all this fussing. Come
on, just get her down there
already!

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Yes, yes, I get it! But if I
judge it to be too dangerous,
I'm bringing her back
immediately! Be careful!
Well, if Euwin is alright, let's\nmove forward.

If that explosion from earlier
was the sound of Euwin's
friend fighting, we should be
close by now.
...Yeah!
It's freezing! This is bad! This is\nso bad!! I'm gonna die!!

I didn't hear about this! What is
that thing?! What happened to
the Kingdom Knights'
intelligence?! Eek!
Over there!
It's coming this way!
